steps.title: Classification
steps.content: This question addresses whether a classical Ayurvedic churna can receive intellectual property protection through a patent. This matters because traditional medicinal knowledge is protected against misappropriation and is legally barred from being patented.

steps.title: Legal position
steps.content: Under Section 3(p) of the patent provisions, an invention which in effect is traditional knowledge, or an aggregation or duplication of known properties of a traditionally known component, is not an invention and is not patentable the cited source. Traditional knowledge already existing cannot be patented the cited source.

steps.title: Protection / action route
steps.content: Instead of patenting, Indian traditional medicinal formulations are protected against misappropriation at International Patent Offices through the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) the cited source. Patent Examiners use the TKDL and other resources to investigate and ensure that traditionally known subject matter is not granted a patent the cited source.
